# Dynamic reports test fixtures

Referenced by spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-dynamic-report-builder-design.md` §6.1/§8 and
`docs/PC02_Report_Builder_Design_Package/UAT-COVERAGE.md`. Regenerate the derived files with:

```bash
python backend/test/fixtures/dynamic-reports/generate-oracle.py
python backend/test/fixtures/dynamic-reports/generate-hostile.py
```

Both scripts are idempotent and only touch `real/*.json` and `hostile/*.xlsx`; the real workbooks
under `real/*.xlsx` are copied from production/legacy samples and must never be regenerated.

## real/ — genuine production-style workbooks

| File | Source | Why it's a fixture |
|---|---|---|
| `hsln_17_sheets.xlsx` | `docs/PC02_Report_Builder_Design_Package/excel report/` | 17 sheets (TỔNG + 16 team sheets), 33 unlocked input cells/sheet with sample numbers (no tokens — tests the "unlocked+literal → warn, don't block" rule), 258 rows. TỔNG has 228 `=SUM('Đội 3:Cơ sở 2'!C<n>)` 3-D formulas, of which **190 cache `#REF!`** because the Tổ 10 sheet is upstream-corrupted — see `real/hsln-oracle.json` and spec §10 R11. This is the primary aggregate-engine oracle. |
| `hsln-oracle.json` | generated by `generate-oracle.py` from the file above | Per-TỔNG-row independent sum (ignoring the workbook's own stale cache), for asserting the `aggregate` engine without circular trust in either the workbook or the engine under test. |
| `bao_cao_ngay_shared_formulas.xlsx` | `docs/pc02hcm.com-new/public_html/uploads/excel/bao_cao_ngay.xlsx` | 211 cells use Excel's `t="shared"` master-formula compression — the parser (PR3, review finding R3) must expand shared formulas, not just read `f.formula` on cells that happen to hold the master copy. |
| `a09_1034_unlocked.xlsx` | legacy `XuatBaoCao/excel_templates/template_20250813_085927_...xlsx` | 1,034 unlocked cells, 22 formulas, 56×39 merges — stress case for the "unlocked cell with no token → warning, not error" rule at scale. |
| `a10_99_formulas.xlsx` | legacy `.../template_20250826_142229_...xlsx` | 99 formulas, 455 unlocked cells, 33 merges — second independent sample for the parser/formula-classification golden tests. |
| `pl7.xlsx` | legacy `.../bieu_mau/PL7.xlsx` | Small single-sheet real BCA template — baseline "simple" golden case. |
| `phu_luc_07_08_multi_sheet.xlsx` | `docs/Mẫu BC tháng/Mẫu phụ lục 07, 08.xlsx` | Two sheets, 47–52 merges each, 5–10 formulas — multi-sheet selection + merge-anchor golden case. |
| `phu_luc_1_6_merges.xlsx` | `docs/Mẫu BC tháng/Mẫu phụ lục 1-6.xlsx` | Six sheets, up to 37 merges, zero formulas, zero unlocked cells — "every cell is static, publish should warn there is no input" golden case. |

## hostile/ — synthetic malicious/malformed uploads

Generated by `generate-hostile.py`, each still named `*.xlsx` (attacker renames the extension), so
tests assert the guard inspects **content**, not the filename:

| File | Attack simulated | Expected rejection point |
|---|---|---|
| `password_encrypted.xlsx` | MS-OFFCRYPTO password-encrypted workbook | `assertMagicBytes` — real encrypted .xlsx is an OLE2/CFBF container, not a ZIP; no `PK\x03\x04` header |
| `renamed_macro_as_xlsx.xlsx` | `.xlsm` macro-enabled workbook saved with `.xlsx` extension | Content-type/`vbaProject.bin` presence check in `TemplateService`, after `assertMagicBytes` passes (it IS a valid zip) |
| `external_link.xlsx` | Formula referencing another workbook via `xl/externalLinks/` | Parser external-link detection (FRD §4.3) |
| `zip_bomb.xlsx` | 305 KB compressed → 300 MB (1 member, ratio ~1029×) | `assertNoZipBomb` (`XLSX_LIMITS.MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO = 100`) |
| `eight_sheets_select_limit.xlsx` | Valid, non-hostile 8-sheet workbook | Not rejected at upload (file-level `XLSX_LIMITS.MAX_SHEET_COUNT = 20`); selecting all 8 as *report* sheets must be rejected by the dynamic-reports-specific ≤5-selected-sheet limit (spec §10 R6) — selecting ≤5 of the 8 must succeed |

Oversized-byte-count fixtures (>10 MB / >100 MB per spec §4.3) are deliberately **not** committed as
binary blobs — PR3's tests build those in-memory at test time (repeat a cell value programmatically)
to keep the repo small; see spec §10 R6 for the two-tier limit (file-level vs. selected-report-level).
